caption:
It’s very clear to me that we are being poisoned from as many angles as possible. Electromagnetic frequency (EMF) is no exception.

If they can set the limits for smart meters this high, we should be cautious about all sources of electromagnetic energy. 

It’s supposed to be highly regulated to protect human health, but learning this is troubling.

Now consider that they want smart devices everywhere monitoring everything you do, thus we will be bombarded by even more EMF. 

It’s poisoning on a cellular level. 

#SmartMeter #EMFRadiation #HealthEffects #ElectromagneticPollution #RegulatoryFailure PublishedScience MicrowaveRadiation PowerDensity SafetyStandards RadiationExposure
audio_track_actual: Narration lifted from the documentary 'Take Back Your Power' (2017, Josh del Sol), a smart-meter clip. Male narrator reads a ladder of radio-frequency power-density values (µW/cm²) against claimed biological effects, framed as 'published science.'
video_overlay_text_observed: Cover card: 'Learn about safe electromagnetic radiation levels. Smart meters and 5G towers at schools makes no sense. Kids don't need this.' On-screen source credit: 'From "Take Back Your Power 2017 — smart meter documentary".' A 'MP' watermark.
audio_content_summary: Presents a power-density ladder (in µW/cm²) each tied to a biological effect said to be from published science: 0.2 billionths = minimum cell-phone signal; 0.00027 = pine needles age prematurely; 0.05 = children 8-17 get headaches/irritation/concentration/behavioral problems; 0.1 = Building Biology 'extreme concern' guideline; 1.0 = sperm DNA fragmentation in vitro plus a symptom list (headaches, dizziness, fatigue, insomnia, chest pain, breathing difficulty, indigestion); 2.5 = altered calcium in heart-muscle cells; 4.0 = hippocampus/memory-learning changes; 6.0 = DNA damage. Then measurements/standards: EPRI (Dec 2010) measured an Itron smart meter at up to 7.93; 'our own testing' ~8.0 at one foot; Switzerland/Liechtenstein/Luxembourg set 9.5 and China/Poland/Russia 10.0; a room of 12 meters tested 19.8; and the US/Canada safety limit is 600-1000 — argued to be 'tens of thousands of times higher' than levels shown to harm health.
implied_frame: That peer-reviewed science has established biological harm at power densities thousands of times below the smart-meter and regulatory exposure limits, so the limits represent a regulatory failure / deliberate poisoning. Traced (three subagent fact-checks): the effect-threshold ladder is Ronald M. Powell's 2013 re-tabulation of the 2012 BioInitiative Report (an advocacy compilation); the underlying studies are real but the µW/cm² thresholds are unit-substitutions — most papers measured SAR (W/kg) or field strength (V/m), not incident power density — and several rows are misattributed (the 4.0 'hippocampus memory' row cites a 1988 chick-muscle ion-channel study; the 0.05 children figure is a dosimeter detection floor whose authors called the association non-causal) or omit on-point double-blind nulls (Eltiti 2007). Assessed in [[2017-emf-bioeffect-chart-001]]. The regulatory limits the clip cites are documented in [[2017-emf-exposure-limits-001]]: the 600-1000 µW/cm² US/Canada figure is stated correctly (a thermal, 30-min-averaged limit — a different basis from the non-thermal effect claims), but the EPRI 7.93 figure is a misread (a percent-of-limit value relabeled as µW/cm²) and two country groupings are wrong (Luxembourg stricter, China looser than stated).
